question: How can I find out who owns a given land parcel in Spain: which register holds ownership, whether it is open, and the legal route and cost to obtain it?

answer.summary: Legal ownership is held by the Registro de la Propiedad (Colegio de Registradores, under the Ministerio de Justicia). It is not open data: a nota simple (9,02 EUR per finca online, plus VAT) names the registered titular if you state a legitimate interest; the registrar decides within 24 h. Catastro shows the fiscal 'titular catastral' only to the owner or authorised persons (free online); its open data has no owner. No bulk owner dataset was found.
main_caveats: Registro and Catastro can disagree: Catastro data are presumed true only 'sin perjuicio del Registro' (TRLCI art. 3.3). Land never inscribed has no registry entry; Catastro then names only a fiscal titular.

Price conflict: BOE-consolidated arancel (RD 1427/1989) sets 3,005061 EUR per nota simple; the Colegio charges 9,02 EUR online (doctrine DGRN). A 2026 draft RD would codify 9,02; not confirmed in force.
Registry information is for the requester's own use for the stated interest; the sede terms forbid redistribution or loading it into searchable databases.

Navarra (Registro de la Riqueza Territorial) and Araba, Bizkaia, Gipuzkoa run their own cadastres: the state Catastro certificate does not cover them and rules differ (Bizkaia: valor catastral not protected).
Public-notice route (BOE expropriation lists) gives owners only for parcels hit by a project, for the notice period, and with 'Desconocido' for some parcels.
answer.confidence_reason: Legal route, access rules and fees read on official pages and BOE; the actual nota simple order flow was not run (payment, SPA) and the 9,02 vs 3,01 price conflict is unresolved.

attributes.note: Registro de la Propiedad = legal title; Catastro = fiscal titular catastral (art. 3.3 TRLCI: Registro prevails). Navarra and Basque provinces have own cadastres.
Not open: registry needs interes legitimo; Catastro titular is protected data; open parcel data has no owner. Registradores open-data portal blocked to my client.
Nota simple/certificacion from any registrar; Catastro certificate by owner, authorised person, heir; BOE expropriation notices list owners; denial appealable to DGSJFP.
Nota simple 9,02 EUR online (BOE arancel says 3,01 in person); Catastro online free, Gerencia 17,97 EUR; Navarra cedula 6,20; Araba 3,44. Bizkaia/Gipuzkoa fees not found.
attributes.gap_note: Fees of Bizkaia and Gipuzkoa certificates and any post-2021 Navarra tariff change were not found on the pages opened.

how_to_use.example_request: Order in the sede (no automated order made): https://sede.registradores.org/sede/sede-corpme-web/home/ > Propiedad > Nota simple; search by CRU, finca number, cadastral reference (only for fincas coordinated with Catastro), titular name/NIF or address; state interes legitimo; pay by card.
how_to_use.example_result: Not obtained: ordering needs payment and a stated interest. The sede terms say the nota simple gives 'su identificación con indicación del Código Registral Único (CRU), la identidad del titular o titulares de derechos inscritos'.
steps: Get the cadastral reference of the parcel (Catastro non-protected web service Consulta_RCCOOR by coordinates, source 2) to identify it.
Request a nota simple on the Colegio sede (or in person at the registry of the finca) giving CRU, finca number, cadastral parcel or address, and state a legitimate interest.
The registrar answers within 24 h granting or denying; if denied, the amount is refunded and the decision can be appealed before the DGSJFP.
If the parcel is not found, request a nota de localizacion by titular NIF to find registry, CRU and nature of rights; or a certificacion negativa to prove no inscribed finca.
Use a certificacion (arancel-based fee), not a nota simple, when proof with legal faith is needed.
reading_traps: Price conflict: registradores.org and sede terms say 9,02 EUR per nota simple; the BOE-consolidated arancel (RD 1427/1989, Numero 4.1.f) says 3,005061 EUR per nota simple; e-Justice (updated 2024-02-26) says 3,01 EUR + VAT in person and 9,02 EUR + VAT online.
A 2026 Ministerio de Justicia draft RD would add 9,02 EUR for the telematic nota simple to the arancel; the memoria says it is currently minuted under DGRN doctrine; not confirmed in force.
Nota simple 'no da fe': only a certificacion proves content. Fees exclude VAT/IGIC/IPSI.
A registered owner can differ from the titular catastral; unregistered land returns no finca.

problems: Order flow requires payment and a stated interest and was not run.
opendata.registradores.org (the ordering portal named by e-Justicia) returned 'Request Rejected' to curl and WebFetch: rejects automated clients.

steps: Find the RC from coordinates: GET https://ovc.catastro.meh.es/ovcservweb/OVCSWLocalizacionRC/OVCCoordenadas.asmx/Consulta_RCCOOR?SRS=EPSG:25830&Coordenada_X=540350&Coordenada_Y=4579710 returned RC 0001001 00WL47G (EPSG:25830; EPSG:4326 also accepted).
Free open view (Consulta_DNPRC or the sede page): location, use, surface; the sede page shows 'Acceso datos protegidos' instead of the owner.

To see the titular: owner logs in with certificado/Cl@ve/clave concertada in the Sede and downloads a certificate (online certificates carry no tasa); a third party needs the owner's signed authorisation (model on the assistant page), or is heir, holder of a real right or adjoining owner.
In Gerencias or Puntos de Informacion Catastral the tasa de acreditacion catastral applies (4,52 EUR literal + 4,52 per property; 17,97 EUR descriptiva y grafica).
Take the RC (certificate or parcel) to the registry request (source 1) to get the registered owner.
reading_traps: The open web services and the INSPIRE parcel ATOM downloads (Adradas 42005: 3426 parcels, fields areaValue, nationalCadastralReference, geometry) contain no owner.
Titular catastral may differ from the registered owner and may be outdated; Registro prevails.
Catastro coverage excludes Navarra and Pais Vasco: the ATOM index lists 52 territorial offices without 01, 20, 31, 48.

problems: Protected owner data need digital certificate, Cl@ve or authorisation: not tested.
Consulta_RCCOOR with EPSG:4326 returned error 16 'no hay referencia' at -3.7038,40.4168 but an RC at -3.7070,40.4169.

recipe: Get the RC of the parcel from coordinates or polygon/parcel with the free Catastro web services (Consulta_RCCOOR tested; Consulta_DNPPP listed on the service page).
If you are the owner (or hold written authorisation), download the Catastro certificate from the Sede to read the titular catastral; in Navarra and Basque provinces use the foral cadastre.
Otherwise ask any registrar for a nota simple stating the legitimate interest; search by RC (if the finca is coordinated) or by address, then read titular and charges.
For parcels touched by public projects, search the BOE Section V-B notice and extract the table with pdftotext -layout (tested on BOE-B-2026-33524).

open_questions: Which price applies to an online nota simple: 9,02 EUR (Colegio, DGRN doctrine) or 3,005061 EUR (arancel in BOE)? The 2026 draft RD would settle it; whether it has been approved was not found.
How the registrar judges 'interes legitimo' for a stranger to the parcel is decided case by case; only the DGSJFP appeal outcome can answer it.

history.note: Ownership sits in the Registro de la Propiedad (paid, per finca, legitimate interest) and, as titular catastral, in the Catastro (protected data); no open owner dataset found.
